# Current release · Keystone Polygon experience R6 · 2026-11-14 · revised 2026-11-15

index.html is a ten-chapter story in 29 scenes about one real Eagle County, Colorado parcel (220531300003, 4.235 ha, a historical screening candidate). Direct route ?chapter=ID with optional &step=ID. Chapters · polygon, living, engine, spillover, measured, clock, forecast, windows, obligation, next.

A Keystone Polygon is a parcel whose condition and position shape what happens to people and places well beyond its boundary, a name it earns only when an active function, a pathway across the boundary and a recipient who would feel its loss have each been shown. No Colorado parcel is validated as one. Keystone function, pathway, recipient, rights, payer and financial return are all unestablished for this parcel.

The story shows the parcel as a node in a dependency graph that runs from land through living communities, ecosystem processes and pathways to recipients, consequences and an obligation. Each scene that presents evidence is tagged Computed, Observed, Tested, Published elsewhere, Illustrative, Pending or Assessed. Published ecology comes from other places and is unmeasured on the parcel. Each scene keeps its method, limits and sources in labelled expanders. The spillover chapter computes two kinds of connection in the reader's browser from public data. Water over terrain follows the steepest descent on a 30 m elevation model and is tagged Computed. Movement of forest-dwelling animals, pollinating insects and wetland and stream-side species between habitat patches is modelled from 2023 USGS land cover and USDA Forest Service tree canopy and is tagged Illustrative, since none of these groups has been surveyed or tracked here. The parcel's importance to that movement is measured as the fall in equivalent connected habitat area when its cover is cleared. Terrain results describe the shape of the surface, carry no measured flow and stop at the edge of an elevation window about 30 km across, short of the Colorado River. The one held forecast result, a 6.84% lower log-scale error at North Inlet, is 1.4% on the raw scale and was a borderline pass among five pre-registered tests, and the other four failed. The historical screening score of 0.6724 rested mostly on placeholder attributes and is kept only as an archived artifact. North Inlet, East Inlet and the Glenwood station are separate cases with no traced delivery from the parcel. No atmospheric transport.

The framework generates machine-readable records for agents (a dependency graph, an evidence passport, a claim register, a reference register, a data inventory and a release manifest with integrity hashes). The pages draw on display versions of the graph, the passport, the references and the layer inventory that hold only what the pages show. The claim register, the release manifest, the complete records and the core methods are held by Graph of Life and shared on request.

passport.html is the candidate file. review.html is the historical monitoring budget review, and it recomputes the SHA-256 of each monitoring record it loads and shows the record as verified only when the hash matches. The round-two display records name their models and policies descriptively, and the frozen records behind them keep their internal identifiers. evidence.html and legacy.html are earlier releases kept for the record.
